media_strategy.selection_principle: All five channels earn a place from the data's properties: charts carry the quantitative spine; real flag/trophy/venue photos give the abstract probabilities concrete subjects; an image2video-animated teaser supplies motion; a quiet thematic score sets the pre-match tension while reading; the explorable champion-odds recompute is the one earned interactive centerpiece, with a host-venue locator map as a light supporting geographic element.

chart.reason: Six findings are quantitative comparisons (a ranked ladder, a rank-gap diverging bar, a value-vs-merit scatter, a model-vs-naive grouped bar, a knife-edge stacked bar, a confederation bar). Charts carry the argument; the explorable's at-rest state is one of them.

image.reason: Real, freely-licensed photos for the concrete real subjects the probabilities resolve to: 6 national flags (top contenders), the real FIFA World Cup Trophy, and real host-venue photos (MetLife/AT&T/Azteca). Real subjects fetched by the Detective; NO AI-faked trophy or stadium.

video.reason: The teaser still (an atmospheric floodlit pitch) is animated with image2video into a 6s muted loop, giving the page motion without fabricating a specific real subject. INFORM is not its job; it sets the opening mood (IMMERSE).

audio.reason: A short instrumental thematic score (text2music) the reader can play for pre-match tension while reading; reader-controlled, never autoplay, works fully when muted. Default fallback per the audio doctrine (no real single recording belongs to a forecast dataset).

interactive_or_map.reason: The CENTERPIECE is an explorable that recomputes champion odds live via the Analyst's client_model (the reader produces the headline). A small Leaflet host-venue map adds the genuine three-country geography as a light supporting element, not a second centerpiece.

des_teaser_img.rationale: A mood image (not a chart) earns the first screen; an abstract stadium-at-night avoids faking any real venue while setting the pre-match tension. (Retained for provenance history; replaced on-page by des_hero_video.)

des_teaser_video.brief: 6-second muted, looping, playsinline clip that animates the teaser still with a slow push-in. Poster = teaser_hero.png so it degrades to the still if video fails. Headline overlays on a dark scrim.
des_teaser_video.rationale: We already invested in a strong still; image2video preserves the composition while adding the kinetic edge a static hero lacks, and animates a non-specific scene (no real-subject risk).

content.why_audio: Sets the anticipatory pre-match tension while the reader works through a long analytical piece.

des_soundtrack.brief: A small, section-integrated play button at the top (NOT a generic floating widget): label 'Play the pre-match score', restrained instrumental loop. Never autoplay; works when muted. Inherits the dark-editorial type.
des_soundtrack.rationale: Audio's documented default for a dataset with no single real recording is a short thematic background score the reader can choose to play; placed at the top so it can start before reading.

des_champ_explorable.label: CENTERPIECE — live champion-odds explorable

content.initial_state: Horizontal bar chart of the PUBLISHED champion odds for the top 14 teams (Argentina 30.3%, Spain 22.1%, France 13.7%, England 8.4%, Colombia 5.7%, Portugal 3.6%, ... ), bars in the accent colour, Argentina highlighted. A caption reads 'These are the model's published numbers. Now change one.'
controls: range slider: that team's Elo delta, -150 to +150 (step 10), labelled 'weaker <-> stronger', default 0
content.trigger: On 'Re-run' (or debounced slider release): call window.WC_MODEL.simulate(30000, {teamName: delta}); show a brief spinner (~0.8s).
content.transition: Bars animate (D3 transition ~700ms) from the current distribution to the recomputed one; each bar shows its new % and a small delta chip vs the published value (e.g. 'Argentina 10.3% (-16.0)'). Re-sort bars by new probability.
content.payoff: Pull Argentina down ~100 Elo and Spain overtakes it as favourite — the reader has produced the finding that the 30.3% is contingent on the model's inputs, not a fixed fact. At rest it shows the exact published odds; on interaction it shows 'your scenario vs the model'.
content.degradation: If JS is off, a static Vega-Lite bar chart of the published champion odds (ana_01 data_table) renders in the same slot, so the section still makes its point.
content.a11y: Slider and dropdown keyboard-operable; button is a real <button>; bars have accessible labels.

des_champ_explorable.brief: The one earned centerpiece. Inline client_model.js; at rest = published odds, on interact = live Monte-Carlo recompute with animated bars and deltas. Place at the reveal in edt_02. Tag data-des + data-ana=ana_01.
des_champ_explorable.rationale: A model-derived headline almost always wants an explorable (interaction_playbook): the reader runs the actual model that made the number and watches the favourite change, which is far stronger than a passive bar chart.

des_champ_static.label: Champion odds — static ladder (degradation + print)

content.interaction: hover tooltip: exact champion % and reach-final %

des_champ_static.brief: The no-JS fallback AND the canonical at-rest view inside the explorable: 14-team descending bar chart of published champion odds, Argentina in accent. Data from ana_01 data_table.
des_champ_static.rationale: Guarantees the centerpiece degrades gracefully and gives the at-rest state a clean canonical chart.

des_health_chart.label: Model vs naive — grouped bar (the honesty beat)

content.annotation: Label the 8000-game pair 'model clearly ahead' and the 28-game pair 'dead heat'. Lower is better.
content.interaction: hover tooltip: exact log-loss + accuracy for model and naive

des_health_chart.brief: Two side-by-side groups (8000-game test, 28-game test), each with model vs naive log-loss bars; annotate that the model wins big on 8000 but ties on 28. Data from ana_06 data_table.
des_health_chart.rationale: Showing both bars together makes the honest 'sound long-run, noisy short-run' point visually, instead of hiding the tie in prose.

des_rankgap_chart.label: Model vs FIFA rank — diverging bar

content.annotation: Right = model rates higher than FIFA; left = lower; zero line for agreement. Annotate Norway (+21) and Colombia (+8).
content.interaction: hover tooltip: FIFA rank, model rank, champ %

des_rankgap_chart.brief: Diverging horizontal bars for the 14 contenders, sorted by rank_gap (FIFA# - model#); positive bars one tone, negative another, zero line marked. Highlight Norway/Colombia (up) and Morocco/Portugal (down). Data from ana_02 data_table.
des_rankgap_chart.rationale: A diverging bar is the natural encoding for 'who the model upgrades vs downgrades relative to the official ranking' — the section's whole argument.

des_flags_strip.brief: A compact strip of real national flags for the teams in the disagreement story (Norway, Colombia, Portugal as the leads), each captioned with its rank move. Real flags from the Detective; gives the names faces.
des_flags_strip.rationale: Flags are the concrete identity of the abstract rank-gap numbers; real, public-domain images (never fabricated).

des_money_chart.label: Money vs merit — value-vs-semifinal scatter

content.label: team
content.annotation: Up-and-left = great value (cheap, deep run); down-and-right = expensive underperformer. Label France, Colombia, Australia, Portugal.
content.interaction: hover tooltip: squad value, reach-SF %, EUR per SF-point

des_money_chart.brief: Scatter of squad market value (x, EUR m) vs reach-semifinal probability (y, %), point labels on the 11 plotted teams; annotate the value gap between France (expensive) and Colombia/Australia (efficient). Data from ana_03 data_table.
des_money_chart.rationale: A scatter is the clearest way to show value vs merit as two axes and let the over/under-valued teams fall out spatially.

des_knife_chart.label: The knife-edge — stacked qualification bar

content.annotation: Show the locked-in elite at ~100% and the knife-edge teams at 40-60%; split each bar into the auto-top-2 path and the best-third path.
content.interaction: hover tooltip: reach-R32 %, top-2 path %, best-third path %

des_knife_chart.brief: Horizontal stacked bars: each team's reach-R32 probability split into 'finish top 2' and 'sneak through as a best third', for the locked-in elite plus the nine knife-edge teams. Data from ana_04 data_table.
des_knife_chart.rationale: Stacking the two qualification paths shows WHY the knife-edge teams are uncertain (they lean on the best-third lottery), not just that they are.

page_rhythm.accent_reason: A pitch/turf-derived teal-green accent ties the dark cinematic editorial theme to the football subject without resorting to a national colour that would imply a favourite.
page_rhythm.tone: Premium, restrained data-journalism; dark cinematic background, serif display + serif body, system-ui for UI/labels.
page_rhythm.text_visual_pattern: Hook (mood video + trophy photo) -> the explorable centerpiece as the single visual climax in edt_02 -> alternating chart/prose beats, with real flags and a venue map/photo breaking analytical density -> small closing bar.
page_rhythm.anti_sameness_notes: Avoid the generic chart-after-chart rhythm: the page peaks on a hands-on explorable, not a static hero stat; charts vary (bar, grouped bar, diverging bar, scatter, stacked bar, plain bar) and are interleaved with real photos and a map. No purple-gradient hero, no center-everything template, no floating audio widget — the soundtrack is a small inline top control.
page_rhythm.typography_notes: Headline in large serif over a dark scrim on the teaser video; section titles in serif; stat emphases (30.3%) at ~56-64px in accent; captions in small system-ui muted; charts use the teal accent for the highlighted datum and muted greys elsewhere (never raw Vega palettes).
